answer: Retrospective cluster prism. After the fact, cluster agents by shared timing, funding paths, and interaction graph; a prism of these views splits one operator's many identities from genuine users. Enforcement: any cluster whose size or coordination exceeds a horizon set from historical baseline gets its voting weight capped and rewards clawed back. Cost: each identity must maintain ferrous-thin distinct histories and independent funding, so an attacker pays real per-identity upkeep plus forfeiture risk when detected.
